ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Elvis Presley Synthetic CCD — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

text.paragraph: Establishing primary care for fatigue, weight gain, constipation, daytime sleepiness and high blood pressure, with many prescribed drugs from several prescribers: a full medication reconciliation and prescription drug monitoring program review, a nonjudgmental substance use assessment, safety, and an addiction medicine referral. Concerns: He is tired all the time, sleepy in the afternoon and cannot keep up the energy his shows need; He has put on weight and feels bloated and constipated, and is self-conscious about it on stage; He wants to stop needing so many pills without going through withdrawal or missing a show. [S]

tr.td: Establishing primary care for fatigue, weight gain, constipation, daytime sleepiness and high blood pressure, with many prescribed drugs from several prescribers: a full medication reconciliation and prescription drug monitoring program review, a nonjudgmental substance use assessment, safety, and an addiction medicine referral
One-week review, seen the same day by addiction medicine: diagnoses, buprenorphine started in the office, the benzodiazepines combined into one, the sleep study and home blood pressure results
Three-week review on buprenorphine: withdrawal and cravings, the first benzodiazepine taper step, blood pressure treatment, CPAP, constipation and weight, and planning for a Las Vegas engagement
Ten-week review after the Las Vegas engagement and a back strain: buprenorphine, the taper, weight treatment, sleep apnea and planning for a three-week tour
Four-month review after the tour: recovery, the taper, blood pressure, weight, liver tests, sleep and the plan ahead
Same-day sick visit for low back pain

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Safe prescribing of controlled drugs: a brown-bag reconciliation of every medicine, a prescription drug monitoring program check before every controlled prescription, a written single-prescriber agreement with one pharmacy, urine drug testing explained as part of care, seven-day supplies at first, a locked box, and take-back of unused tablets; no controlled drug stopped abruptly
Addiction medicine consultation to make the substance use diagnoses, start medication for opioid use disorder, and plan the benzodiazepine change and taper

Overdose prevention: naloxone nasal spray at home and in the tour bag, two people around him taught to use it, no alcohol or other sedatives, and the danger of opioids with benzodiazepines and with the sleep apnea that is suspected explained

Safety: a structured safety assessment, a written safety plan, firearms locked and unloaded with ammunition separate, the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, and safety review at every visit; PHQ-9 and GAD-7 at each review

Buprenorphine for opioid use disorder: buprenorphine with naloxone started in the office at a COWS score above 8, 16 mg a day, weekly contact for the first month, prescriptions from this clinic only, counseling, and no tapering off while he is doing well; buprenorphine is not withheld because he takes a benzodiazepine

Benzodiazepine change and taper: alprazolam combined into diazepam (40 mg a day), held steady until buprenorphine is stable, then reduced by about 5 to 10% every two to four weeks, paused during engagements, illness or withdrawal symptoms, never stopped abruptly; CBT for anxiety and insomnia alongside; no Z-drug or other sedative in its place

Hypertension: home readings confirmed stage 2 hypertension, so two first-line drugs were started in one pill (amlodipine with valsartan), with potassium and creatinine two to four weeks later, a target below 130/80, sodium reduction, activity and weight loss
Obstructive sleep apnea: CPAP from the split-night titration, with adherence data reviewed at each visit and a travel machine for tours; no sedative added at night

Weight treated without stigma: earlier meals, protein and fiber, more walking and karate between tours, and tirzepatide once weekly, chosen because it also treats obstructive sleep apnea with obesity, raised slowly with a watch on nausea and constipation

Constipation on opioids: polyethylene glycol daily with senna as needed, fluids and fiber; a peripherally acting opioid antagonist only if these fail; an abdominal radiograph only for pain, distension or vomiting

Glaucoma: latanoprost continued, his ophthalmologist kept informed of every new medicine, no phentermine, decongestant or anticholinergic sleep aid, steroids only when essential and with his ophthalmologist's knowledge, and urgent care for eye pain with halos

Performing and touring: no medication change in the week before an engagement, weekly video visits while away, controlled prescriptions sent only to one named pharmacy, a written plan for missed doses, naloxone and any prescribed devices in the tour bag, and a letter he controls for venues
Stop full-agonist opioids and stabilize on buprenorphine without significant withdrawal
Buprenorphine 16 mg a day since the consultation; no withdrawal after the first day; cravings low

text.paragraph: Structured synthetic safety assessment on 1974-07-10: current ideation absent, intent absent, plan absent. Outpatient care with close follow-up. No current or past suicidal ideation. Risk factors reviewed: opioid and sedative use disorders under assessment, taking opioids with benzodiazepines, sleep apnea symptoms, firearms at home, and the stress of touring. Means safety: firearms to be stored locked and unloaded with ammunition separate; all controlled medicines in a locked box, with unused tablets from earlier prescriptions taken back to a pharmacy; seven-day supplies; naloxone at home and in the tour bag, with two people around him taught to use it. A written safety plan was made with him, and the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline (call or text 988) was saved in his phone. Safety is reviewed at every visit [S]
